## INCIDENT — `/tmp/sig-p3765a` deleted mid-leg; rebuilt byte-identically

Between ~05:00Z (the integrity manifest was last read from
`/tmp/sig-p3765a/work/releases/<pub>/` successfully) and 06:31Z the
whole `/tmp/sig-p3765a` dir — the built work tree AND attempt-2's kept
`work-refused-stalegen` residue — was deleted (the `/tmp` parent mtime
is inconclusive; the agent did not delete it — recorded, never hidden).
The `sites --apply` attempt at 06:31Z refused `[no-release]` on the
empty path — the refusal is how the loss surfaced. The rehearsal
scratch's `r/`, `release/`, `releases/<pub>` were symlinks into the lost
tree (only `release.json`, `s/`, `v/` survive it), so the in-flight
tree-mode verify suite was killed (no result rows had been written —
nothing false recorded).

Recovery — `build_release` was invoked **directly** (not `verb_build`:
no journal write, no lock — `built` is already journaled as 000007) with
every descriptor input pinned to the recorded values:
`built_at=2026-11-25T17:59:06Z`, `code.commit=ac52d33e9ffb…`,
`code.tree=3ee221d8cc6c…` (`git rev-parse ac52d33e^{tree}`),
`environment=production`, `label=sig-2026-11-25.1`,
`template_fingerprint=58eb608c…` — all from the surviving
`sig.site-release/1` release.json copies + attempt-2's ledger row (no
`--boundaries-root` was passed). `git diff ac52d33e..HEAD` over every
release-shaping path shows only `ops/` + `web/` deltas (the two fixes
under test); `exports/` is untouched → the builder emits identical
bytes. Identity is proven cryptographically, not assumed: pub ==
`p-31371dfb…`, rebuilt `integrity_manifest.json` sha256 == `921bece2…`
(every artifact's sha256+byte_size identical by definition), rebuilt
`release.json` byte-equal to the surviving copies, `routes_sha256` ==
`7fe4c687…` — `docs/build/logs/p37.65a-live-3/rebuild-work.py` is the
driver; its verdict lands below.

projection once the big-object bound below was routed around.
**stage attempt log (verbatim):**
- attempt 1 (07:48:45Z): ~99 obj/s sustained for 70 min (the
  token-caching fix doing its work — attempt-2's bound is gone), then
  `GcsError: write operation timed out` on
  `staged/r/…/c/osm_physical/search_index.sqlite` (**348 MB**) at
  08:58:46Z, rc=1 — **the real bound**: the verb's per-object
  `uploadType=media` single-shot POST has no resumable path and the
  opener timeout is 60 s; this uplink measures **36.9 Mbps**
  (`networkQuality`), so under 32-worker fair-share (~1 Mbps/stream)
  a >~20 MB object stalls the write path past 60 s.
- supervisor v1 bug (mine, recorded): the resume `--break-lock` reason
  was passed unquoted → word-split → attempts 2–6 died on argparse
  (rc=2, the verb never ran). Supervisor v2 passes it as one argv
  element (`stage-supervisor.sh` v2 note).
- attempt 2 (supervisor v2, 09:10:39Z, `--break-lock` quoted correctly):
  the resume contract churned the ~366k already-staged files (~35 min of
  local read+md5 — recorded cost), then died on the **same** sqlite at
  09:49:27Z, rc=1.
- **out-of-band bulk leg (recorded, never hidden):** the >10 MB plan
  objects were listed (`big-objects.txt`, 43 rows) and delivered via
  `gsutil cp -n` (resumable upload — survives stalls; `-n` =
  create-if-absent, never overwrite; `upload-big.sh`, `gsutil-big*.log`).
  Two of my own bugs surfaced and are recorded verbatim: v1 ran from the
  wrong cwd so every relative source path `CommandException`'d
  ("No URLs matched") and logged a misleading rc=0 — **zero of the 43
  landed** (the only out-of-band byte up was the manual absolute-path
  sqlite); and that first manual upload ran with
  `parallel_composite_upload_threshold=150M`, so the 348 MB object
  landed **composite** — `md5_hash: None, component_count: 7` — and the
  verb's resume can never md5-skip a composite object (it would try
  insert → 412 → md5Hash None ≠ local → NameCollision). Fix: the
  composite object was deleted and all 43 were re-uploaded with
  composite disabled (`upload-big.sh` v2) — **43/43 verified present
  with md5Hash** (`gsutil-big2.log`, zero entries in
  `gsutil-big2-failures.txt`). The delete+recreate corrected MY OWN
  out-of-band write (identical bytes, recorded); the pipeline's
  never-overwrite rule was never touched. The verb's contract keeps the
  leg honest regardless: identical names+bytes → `resumed` skips; a byte
  difference → NameCollision — preserved end-to-end.
- attempt 3 (09:49:47Z): died 10:29:59Z on the **same** sqlite — GCS
  only 412s after the request body streams, and the 348 MB body stalls
  before the 412 lands; a raced-into-existence object does NOT save a
  large plan entry (recorded bound).
- attempt 4 (10:30:19Z): killed at ~10:47Z — its pre-captured
  `existing` listing already held the composite sqlite with no md5Hash,
  so the attempt was doomed to the same POST stall; killed before it
  burned the skip phase.
- attempt 5 (11:17:57Z, `--break-lock`): fresh listing sees all 44 big
  objects with md5Hash → skips them; small-object inserts then resume at
  the measured ~99 obj/s → **rc=0 13:36:53Z** (`stage-apply.log` tail:
  `applied pub=p-31371dfb… event=…000009-…`).
